title: Nginx
description: nginx access and error logs from Loki. Only populated where nginx runs (prod, prod.local).

list.name: search
list.label: Search
list.description: Substring filter applied to every panel on this dashboard.

list.name: vhost
list.label: nginx vhost
list.description: Which nginx server block served the request.

list.name: monvhost
list.label: Monitoring vhost
list.description: Grafana's own vhost is excluded by default; its auto-refresh traffic would skew every panel.

list.name: host
list.label: Host header
list.description: Host header the client sent. Unknown hosts collapse into "other"; the log line still shows the raw value.

list.name: nginxlevel
list.label: nginx level
list.description: nginx severity. Defaults to warn and above: nginx writes worker start/reload notices into the error log, and Grafana renders 'notice' as INFO.

panels.title: Requests/s
panels.description: Requests per second across the selected vhosts.

panels.title: Requests (range)
panels.description: Total requests in the dashboard time range.

panels.title: 4xx share

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host", status=~"4.."} [$__range])) / sum(count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} [$__range])) * 100

panels.description: Client errors as a share of all requests.

panels.title: 5xx (range)

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host", status=~"5.."} [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.description: Server errors in the range. Anything above zero is worth a look.

panels.title: p95 response time

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, {job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host", status!="101"} | regexp `"request_time": "(?P<rt>[0-9.]+)"` | unwrap rt [$__auto]) by ()

panels.description: 95th percentile of nginx request_time. Websocket upgrades (101) are excluded, they stay open for hours.

targets.expr: sum(rate({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} | regexp `"body_bytes_sent": "(?P<sent>[0-9]+)"` | unwrap sent [$__auto]))

panels.title: nginx requests/s by status

targets.expr: sum by (status) (rate({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} [$__auto]))

panels.description: From the nginx json access log; empty in dev (no nginx).

panels.title: Top client IPs

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (ip, country, city) (count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} | regexp `"remote_addr": "(?P<ip>[^"]*)"` | regexp `"geoip_city": "(?P<city>[^"]*)"` [$__range])))

panels.description: Busiest source addresses with their GeoIP country and city. nginx faces the internet directly on Hetzner, so remote_addr is the visitor's own IP.

panels.title: Top request URIs

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (path) (count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} | regexp `"request_uri": "(?P<path>[^?"]*)` [$__range])))

panels.description: Busiest paths in the selected range, query strings stripped. Uses a regexp capture rather than | json so only one label is extracted.

panels.title: Top countries

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (country) (count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} [$__range])))

panels.description: GeoIP country of the client, paired with 'Top cities'. 'unknown' covers private/LAN addresses, which is everything outside real prod.

panels.title: Top user agents

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (ua) (count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} | regexp `"http_user_agent": "(?P<ua>[^"]*)"` [$__range])))

panels.description: Busiest clients by User-Agent string. Bots and the picture frames themselves stand out here.

panels.title: Top cities

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (country, city) (count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} | regexp `"geoip_city": "(?P<city>[^"]*)"` [$__range])))

panels.description: GeoIP city of the client, drilling down on 'Requests by country'. Captured at query time rather than as a Loki label, since city is high-cardinality. 'unknown' is expected for a large share of traffic - GeoLite2 city coverage is much thinner than country coverage, especially for IPv6 and mobile ranges.

panels.title: Request origins

targets.expr: topk(50, sum by (ip, country, city, lat, lon) (count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} | json ip="remote_addr", city="geoip_city", lat="geoip_lat", lon="geoip_lon" | lat != "" [$__range])))
topk(20, sum by (country) (count_over_time({job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} [$__range])))

panels.description: Where the traffic comes from. Green dots are GeoIP city coordinates, one per client IP; the blue halos are country centroids covering every request, including the IPs GeoLite2 resolves to a country but no city. 'unknown' has no location and never appears here, so the map stays empty outside real prod. Basemap tiles are fetched by the browser.

panels.title: nginx access log

targets.expr: {job="nginx", logtype="access", server_name=~"$vhost", server_name!~"$monvhost", http_host=~"$host"} |= "$search" | json | line_format "{{.remote_addr}} {{.request_method}} {{.http_host}}{{.request_uri}} -> {{.status}} ({{.request_time}}s, {{.body_bytes_sent}}b) {{.http_user_agent}}"

panels.description: One line per request. Expand a line to see every JSON field.

panels.title: nginx error log
panels.description: nginx-level problems: upstream failures, buffering warnings, TLS issues. Add 'notice' to the level filter to also see worker start/reload lines.
